lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Move the most relevant research, technical skills, and publications higher for quant roles.
items.because: The résumé does not yet make its strongest quant qualifications prominent enough.

items.says: Order bullets within roles by importance, credibility, and relevance.
items.because: The strongest, most verifiable accomplishments should come first.

items.says: Give research outputs a separate, more visible section for research-heavy applications.
items.because: The papers, seminar presentation, and open-source package deserve more visibility.

items.says: Use consistent dates, separators, capitalization, spelling conventions, and bullet punctuation.
Check that wrapped bullets align cleanly in the final PDF.
items.because: Several bullets break awkwardly and may create excessive white space.

items.says: Replace the placeholder-looking website if it is not the actual URL, and link directly to relevant work or a profile.
items.because: A nonfunctional or obviously generic URL undermines the application.

items.says: Consider adding a relevant professional or research profile link.
items.because: A useful LinkedIn, Google Scholar, research page, or GitHub profile could strengthen the contact information.

items.says: Add a useful research focus or degree detail, such as a specialization, advisor, dissertation topic, or coursework.
items.because: The Ph.D. entry currently gives no detail about this important qualification.

items.says: Clarify full-time enrollment if the overlapping employment dates could raise questions.
items.because: The Ph.D. and current job dates overlap.

items.says: Verify and update the expected graduation date if it has changed.
items.because: “Expected May 2026” needs to remain accurate.

items.says: Consider removing the B.S. entry if space is tight.
items.because: For a Ph.D. candidate, it is less important than publications, methods, and technical work.

items.says: Shorten or reduce the bakery role’s visual prominence for quant applications.
items.because: Its relevance is mainly leadership, operational accountability, or employment continuity rather than quant research.

items.says: Specify your scheduling authority, budget size, staffing complexity, or operational result.
items.because: “Managed” and “keeping within budget” are credible but generic without clearer scale and responsibility.

items.says: Give the period over which unsold bread fell from 12% to 7%.
items.because: Without a timeframe, the result is difficult to assess.

items.says: Clarify whether the reduction came solely from your process or a broader initiative.
items.because: “Cutting” may overstate causality if other changes contributed.

items.says: Define the risk-adjusted-return metric and its comparison baseline.
items.because: The 35% improvement is otherwise loosely defined.

items.says: State the evaluation period and whether the result was in-sample, out-of-sample, simulated, or live.
items.because: Without the evaluation design, the major improvement could look overfit.

items.says: Clarify transaction costs and capacity assumptions where relevant.
items.because: They affect how the performance claim should be interpreted.

items.says: Clarify whether this is another presentation of the Sharpe improvement later in the internship entry.
items.because: Multiple versions of one result should not be reported as distinct accomplishments.

items.says: Specify what was purged and why the embargo length was appropriate.
items.because: The stated validation method does not supply those details.

items.says: Clarify whether hyperparameter selection and model evaluation were fully separated.
items.because: Purging and embargoing do not address every source of leakage.

items.says: Qualify the claim that every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: Purging and embargoing do not automatically prove the absence of look-ahead bias.

items.says: Consider giving the number of folds or train/test structure.
items.because: Those details could demonstrate validation rigor.

items.says: Clarify your role in designing the point-in-time safeguards and the technical environment.
items.because: The bullet does not specify those parts of your contribution.

items.says: Verify that “feature store” matches what you implemented.
items.because: A library, pipeline, database, or research framework may need different terminology.

items.says: Confirm that describing reuse in later signal projects complies with Northpeak’s policies.
items.because: Internal project reuse may be confidential.

items.says: Clarify whether the approved live allocation actually occurred and whether you monitored it.
items.because: “Approved” and “live allocation” can attract scrutiny and should not imply an undocumented live result.

items.says: Quantify “small” only if disclosure rules permit.
items.because: The claim should be precise without breaching confidentiality.

items.says: Align the allocation’s timing and your stated involvement with the internship dates.
items.because: An allocation after the internship should not imply continued involvement.

items.says: Confirm that portfolio-manager approval and live-allocation details comply with Northpeak’s policies.
items.because: Those investment details may be confidential.

items.says: Reporting the best Sharpe from 400 backtested configurations as the expected live Sharpe is statistically inappropriate.
items.because: Selection and multiple-testing bias make the search-selected result an unbiased estimate of neither future performance nor a live expectation.

items.says: The order-book signal and 18-month Sharpe result appear duplicated in the Kaggle project.
items.because: The same accomplishment may be claimed twice with inconsistent ownership or results.

items.says: Clarify your ownership, chronology, and exact contribution to the signal.
items.because: “Desk book’s Sharpe ratio” describes portfolio-level impact, while “built a signal” describes individual research.

items.says: Add the benchmark, number of observations or trades, and whether the test period was untouched during development.
items.because: Those details are needed to assess the 18-month out-of-sample claim.

items.says: Confirm that the desk-level performance details comply with Northpeak’s policies.
items.because: Returns and desk information may be confidential.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker can invalidate the Monte Carlo study.
items.because: Workers may generate duplicated or correlated random sequences rather than independent reproducible streams.

items.says: Verify that the speed comparison held simulation quality and hardware constant.
items.because: Those conditions matter to the claimed reduction from three days to five hours.

items.says: Clarify your authorship and contribution without implying the paper was accepted.
items.because: “Under review” is not publication, and the bullet emphasizes the section number over the contribution’s significance.

items.says: Check and specify what “tightens the previous bound by a log factor” means.
items.because: The comparison can be interpreted differently depending on the exact bound.

items.says: Shorten or deprioritize the teaching bullet for industry quant applications.
items.because: It is less relevant than modeling, research, and production-oriented work.

items.says: Identify who gave the 4.8/5 rating and provide the response rate if needed.
items.because: The rating could otherwise look selectively reported.

items.says: Add the R package’s name and a public link.
items.because: The accomplishment is currently difficult to validate.

items.says: Identify the download source and what the 3,000 figure counts.
items.because: Downloads, unique users, and repository events are different measures.

items.says: Consider describing testing, documentation, maintenance, or external adoption.
items.because: Those may be more meaningful than raw downloads.

items.says: Specify the forecast horizon, evaluation period, and data frequency.
items.because: The performance claim needs context to distinguish a robust result from a favorable setup.

items.says: Clarify whether models used identical information sets and tuning procedures, with test data untouched during development.
items.because: The out-of-sample claim depends on how features, architecture, and hyperparameters were selected.

items.says: Clarify whether crisis-period tests were included in the multiple-testing correction.
items.because: Readers may question whether the crisis-period finding was selectively emphasized.

items.says: Explain how forecast-error dependence assumptions were handled.
items.because: They matter to the Diebold-Mariano significance tests.

items.says: Distinguish statistical significance from economic significance.
items.because: A significant QLIKE improvement does not necessarily imply trading value.

items.says: Link the working paper if available and identify your presentation role if there were coauthors.
items.because: Those details better substantiate the research communication claim.

items.says: Replace or supplement the page count with the paper’s title, status, or availability.
items.because: The 12-page length adds little value.

items.says: Add a notable outcome such as rank, score, team result, dataset scale, or technical constraint.
items.because: The current description is generic routine modeling work.

items.says: Explain which direction the validation–leaderboard gap moved.
items.because: “Closed a 0.02 gap” does not say what changed.

items.says: Justify the time-grouped folds rather than treating leaderboard alignment as proof of valid evaluation.
items.because: Closing the gap alone does not establish that the revised validation scheme was correct.

items.says: The order-book signal and 18-month Sharpe claim appear duplicated in the Northpeak internship.
items.because: A professional portfolio impact inside a competition project creates an ownership and credibility problem.

items.says: Confirm that the signal belonged to the Kaggle project and that its data were not reused from the internship.
items.because: The résumé does not explain how the competition result relates to the Northpeak result.

items.says: Confirm you have authority to describe a futures book in this project.
items.because: A professional portfolio claim may be inappropriate or confidential in a competition entry.

items.says: Organize the skills by proficiency or relevance and add applicable tools demonstrated in the experience section.
items.because: Important quant tools or libraries may be missing.

items.says: Support or reconsider the Kafka listing.
items.because: Kafka appears nowhere else and could look like keyword padding.

items.says: Make the depth of PyTorch use clear in the project description.
items.because: The project supports listing it, but does not show how deeply it was used.

items.says: “econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: A typo in a stated area of expertise is particularly damaging.

items.says: Use capitalization and formatting consistent with the other skills category.
Consider adding relevant methods already demonstrated in the résumé.
items.because: Volatility forecasting, time-series validation, point-in-time handling, multiple-testing correction, and statistical learning may better represent the work.
